drafts.title: Front seat thigh support extended and rear legroom at least as good as main competitors
drafts.description: Tall drivers experience longer front-seat thigh support and rear passengers have equal-or-better knee clearance than main competitors so long journeys are more comfortable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat effective thigh support length ≥ 520 mm (measured from seat back to cushion front edge) AND rear knee clearance (legroom) ≥ 940 mm (both measured per OEM dimensional protocol); both targets must be met on a production-intent vehicle within ±5 mm in lab measurement.
assumptions: Current main competitors' rear knee clearance averages ≈ 930 mm; target adds a conservative 10 mm buffer.
Seat cushion extension of +30–40 mm versus today's baseline is ergonomically acceptable and manufacturable without reducing other seat functions.
uncertainties: Actual competitor dimensions may vary by market and body-geometry assumptions; final target may require trade-offs with trunk packaging or structural elements.
Long-term foam settling and cover stretch could change perceived thigh support; durability tests required.

drafts.title: Cup holders fit common bottles and trunk includes a 12 V power outlet for portable coolers
drafts.description: Customers can store large common bottles and travel mugs securely in the cabin cup holders, and use a powered cooler in the trunk via a dedicated 12 V socket.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders retain cylinders with diameters 60–90 mm and heights up to 300 mm securely during 0.5 g lateral acceleration (no tipping or ejection in 10 repeated trials); trunk contains one accessible 12 V socket capable of delivering up to 120 W usable power and operable while the vehicle is parked (tested across 10 units).
assumptions: Common large beverage containers for target markets fall within 60–90 mm diameter and up to 300 mm height.
Providing a 12 V socket in the trunk with up to 120 W is compatible with vehicle electrical architecture and safety requirements.
uncertainties: Different regional accessory plugs and cooler power draws may vary; users with >120 W devices may require adapters or different connector types.
Cup holder geometry that fits large bottles might reduce space for other small items; design trade-offs need verification.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on first attempt
drafts.description: Hands-free tailgate opens on the first foot gesture in typical use so customers do not need multiple attempts to access the trunk.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: First-attempt open success rate ≥ 95% across 50 standardized trials per vehicle (tests include common real-world conditions: varied footwear, footwear occlusion, and stance 20–40 cm behind bumper); average time from successful gesture to latch release < 2.5 seconds.
assumptions: Standardized test routine will be defined (distance, gesture height, obstruction scenarios) and reproducible in lab and outdoor tests.
Sensors and calibration used in successor vehicles will support reliable detection in common clothing and footwear conditions.
uncertainties: Heavy snow/ice or extreme dirt on sensor areas may reduce detection rate; weather-sealing and sensor placement trade-offs may be required.
Interference from nearby pedestrians or other vehicles may affect detection; field testing in busy parking scenarios needed.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with many colors and fine brightness control
drafts.description: Customers can personalize interior ambient lighting with a wide palette and multiple brightness levels so the lighting matches mood and improves perceived quality.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: System offers at least 64 distinct color choices and at least 10 discrete brightness levels; user can save at least three lighting presets; feature accessible and adjustable within the vehicle UI in ≤ 3 taps.
assumptions: Color rendering and brightness levels will be matched to interior materials to avoid glare or color mismatch.
UI will allow intuitive selection and saving of presets without adding cognitive overhead.
uncertainties: Perceived color differences near low brightness may be limited by interior surface reflectivity; validation with real materials required.
Regulatory limits on interior brightness at night (glare) may constrain usable brightness range.

drafts.title: Seat memory restores saved positions reliably
drafts.description: When drivers select a saved seat position, the seat returns to the saved configuration reliably so users do not need to fine-adjust after recall.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Restoration returns seat position to within ±20 mm (linear) and ±2° (angular) of the saved values in 99% of attempts across 50 recall cycles per vehicle, including after ignition off/on and after small manual adjustments.
assumptions: Reference measurement protocol for seat position (key points and angles) is used consistently in tests.
Electrical and actuator tolerances in successor vehicles permit the stated positional repeatability.
uncertainties: Battery voltage or low-temperature conditions could affect actuator precision; endurance testing across temperature range required.
Aftermarket seat covers or heavy personal items on the seat could affect sensor readings.

drafts.title: Flush door handles operate reliably in freezing conditions
drafts.description: Customers can open flush door handles even after freezing weather so doors do not remain stuck in cold climates.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Handles operate successfully in ≥ 95% of trials after exposure to −20 °C ambient with a uniform 5 mm ice layer over the handle area (20 trials per vehicle), without requiring manual de-icing tools.
assumptions: Cold-climate durability testing protocol will include icing cycles representative of customer experience (freezing rain, refreeze).
Mechanical clearances and materials can be adjusted to maintain function at −20 °C without introducing water ingress issues.
uncertainties: Extreme glacier ice or salt-induced corrosion over time could degrade performance; long-term field data needed.
Anti-icing or heating elements may be necessary in some climates and could affect cost and complexity.
